output.name: Ránu
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, he did not cut it clean. The Sun-Kite was still tied to his wrist, so it went up with the others, and its ribbon streamed behind. Ennu had sewn that ribbon from the last of the sail-cloth, long enough to reach the far side of the sky. Mother Hesk saw it going and said nothing, because she was counting. Up in the north, Tilsa the Net Shuttle goes under and over the ribbon and says it is a seam that will not close. Low in the south-east, Sarra the Cut Kite came to cut the ribbon, and could not. Tavo tried to tear it. He failed, and laughed, which is how you will know him. At midsummer the Sun-Kite flies highest, and from the cliffs the ribbon snaps over the water like a wet rag on a line. The old ones say that if you tie a knot in your own hair and hold it to the wind, the Sun-Kite will tug back. Mend your nets while you wait. The ribbon is still long, and the knot still holds.
output.finding: Find the Net Shuttle, Tilsa, in the northern sky, then go one hand-span (about 20°) straight south of it to find the Sun-Kite's ribbon, Ránu.
